OmicIDX collects metadata from SRA, GEO, BioSample and BioProject and
publishes it as Parquet files. `omicidxr` connects DuckDB to those files,
so you can query tens of millions of records with SQL or `dplyr` without
downloading them.

## Connecting

`omicidx_connect()` returns an ordinary DuckDB DBI connection. The
`version` argument picks the release: `"latest"` (the nightly build, the
default), a dated nightly build `"YYYY-MM-DD"` (kept for 30 days), or a
monthly release `"YYYY-MM"`, which is kept long term and is the one to
cite. This vignette pins the October 2026 monthly release so its results
are reproducible.

```{r}
#| label: connect
#| message: false
library(omicidxr)

con <- omicidx_connect("2026-10")
```

## What is in a release

```{r}
#| label: tables
omicidx_tables(con)
```

The `sradb` and `geometadb` schemas follow the tables of the SRAdb and
GEOmetadb packages. `omicidx_describe()` lists a table's columns:

```{r}
#| label: describe
omicidx_describe(con, "sradb.study")
```

## SQL

Any DuckDB SQL works through DBI. Keep exploratory queries small with
`LIMIT`: every query reads remote files.

```{r}
#| label: sql
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT study_accession, study_title
  FROM sradb.study
  WHERE study_type = 'Transcriptome Analysis'
  LIMIT 5")
```

## dplyr

`omicidx_db()` wraps the connection as lazy `dplyr` tables nested by
schema, so `db$sradb$<TAB>` completes table names. Each table is created
when first used, and nothing is read until `collect()`.

```{r}
#| label: db
db <- omicidx_db(con)
db

db$geometadb$gse |>
  dplyr::filter(title %ILIKE% "%single cell%") |>
  dplyr::select(gse, title, submission_date) |>
  head(5) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

## Disconnecting

```{r}
#| label: disconnect
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```
